tier_reason: First-party numbers in the README (mdast table: toMdast({position:false}) ~0.9 ms, toMdast() with position ~1.9 ms, remark mdast-util-from-markdown ~73 ms; wasm HTML 0.90 ms vs markdown-it 4.52 ms and marked 5.20 ms) with public bench code (harness/nopos_bench.mjs, harness/via_mdast_bench.mjs, harness/e2e_bench.mjs) and published wasm build flags, but the CPU is only 'Apple Mac Studio' (chip not stated) and the rustc and Node versions are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README mdast table (CommonMark spec, 198 KB, best-of-15, Node, Apple Mac Studio): sparkdown toMdast({position:false}) ~0.9 ms vs remark (mdast-util-from-markdown) ~73 ms (~80x as printed); with positions kept, toMdast() ~1.9 ms vs ~73 ms (~38x, derived from page data). HTML in Node: sparkdown wasm 0.90 ms vs markdown-it 4.52 ms (5.0x) and marked 5.20 ms (5.7x). Native table: sparkdown wasm 0.93 ms vs native pulldown-cmark 0.68 ms (wasm is 1.37x slower than native pulldown-cmark) and cmark ~1.9 ms (cmark compared CLI-to-CLI on a 16 MB document).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+simd128,+bulk-memory' cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown (features wasm, or ast,wasm for the mdast benchmarks), then wasm-opt -O4 --enable-simd --enable-bulk-memory into harness/sparkdown.wasm (harness/README.md); Rust stable via rustup, version not stated (MSRV 1.95); Node version not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party, one machine (Apple Mac Studio, chip not stated), absolute times machine-specific. The ~80x headline pairs sparkdown's no-position tree against remark, which always emits positions; the like-for-like position-on comparison is ~38x (derived from page data). harness/nopos_bench.mjs times a hand-written wire reader inside the harness (best of 20 batches of 25) rather than the published npm toMdast entry point, and the README table says best-of-15. The harness README is a stale SPIKE document that still reports the wasm mdast path as ~13-23x faster than JS parsing and 537/652 shape matches, while the top README claims deep equality on all 652 examples. The wasm HTML path (0.93 ms) is slower than native pulldown-cmark (0.68 ms); its win is only over JS libraries (markdown-it, marked). The in-repo cargo bench covers only sparkdown vs pulldown-cmark. Very young project (v0.1.0, 27 June 2026, 3 stars, about 46k npm downloads per month per the npm registry search API).

notes: Numbers match the README; the comparison against remark is real and backed by public harness code, but the 80x headline is position-off vs position-on (like-for-like ~38x). Last commit 2026-06-27 confirmed (release 0.1.0), MIT confirmed, npm monthly downloads 46,331 confirmed via registry.npmjs.org search.

tier_reason: The author's own pedersen-bench README shows starknet-rs wasm 228.67 us vs micro-starknet 1.573 ms (6.88x) with public bench code (benches/pedersen_hash, js-bench.ts, scripts/build_bench_wasm.sh) and a stated CPU (Ryzen 9 5950X), but the rustc version is not stated and the two sides run under different harnesses (criterion under wasmer-js vs benchmark.js), so first-party C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo wasi build --bench=pedersen_hash --release (scripts/build_bench_wasm.sh; default release profile, no profile overrides in Cargo.toml); rustc version not stated; criterion 0.4.0 run under wasmer-js 0.4.1; starknet-crypto pinned at rev 76e32ef; micro-starknet pinned at commit a1e7fa0 and timed with benchmark.js 2.1.4 (js-bench.ts, webpack build); Node.js v18.12.1
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark repo by the starknet-rs author, frozen since 22 November 2022 with both implementations pinned to 2022 commits (starknet-crypto rev 76e32ef, micro-starknet a1e7fa0); both have changed a lot since, so the 6.88x is stale. Different harnesses on each side: criterion compiled to wasm32-wasi and run through the wasmer-js WASI shim on Node's V8, versus benchmark.js mean on pure JS whose inputs are hex strings parsed on every call. Single function (pedersen_hash). The same README's native table shows starknet-rs 1.15x slower than pathfinder, whose Pedersen code starknet-crypto credits as its source. Current first-party figures from separate machines are not comparable: the starknet-crypto README gives wasm pedersen_hash 64.96 us on wasmtime 21.0.1 (Apple M3 Max) and the renamed scure-starknet README gives pedersen 883 us/op on an Apple M4 in JS. starknet-crypto has no constant-time guarantees and is not audited (README warning). Last commit 2025-11-09, near the 12-month line, so this entry will turn stale soon.

notes: Numbers and hardware match the pedersen-bench README; the comparison is real but stale (2022 pins) and cross-harness. Metadata confirmed: 312 stars, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, last commit 2025-11-09 (active, borderline). The record's caveat that the wasm did not run in V8 was misleading (wasmer-js runs on Node's WebAssembly engine) and has been reworded.

tier_reason: First-party sample run in README.md and bench/README.md (round-trip N=1024 ~124 vs ~97, N=65536 ~79 vs ~57 MSamples/s against fft.js) with public bench code (bench/run.mjs) and public build flags, but the hardware is only 'Apple Silicon' and the rustc version is not stated, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust (version not stated) for wasm32-unknown-unknown with -C target-feature=+simd128 (.cargo/config.toml); release profile opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort; wasm-opt -O3; scalar variant built with -C target-feature=-simd128 (bench/build-scalar.mjs); bench/run.mjs with 150 ms warmup and 500 ms measurement; Node 25
corrections.claimed_speedup: Round trip with persistent plans (bench/README.md sample run, Apple Silicon, Node 25): tinyfft SIMD ~124 vs fft.js ~97 MSamples/s at N=1024 (~1.28x) and ~79 vs ~57 at N=65536 (~1.39x); forward ~250 vs ~207 at N=1024 (~1.21x) and ~159 vs ~115 at N=65536 (~1.38x), but ~262 vs ~258 at N=256 (a tie); ratios derived from page data. The scalar build (~91 and ~43 MSamples/s round trip) is slower than fft.js at both sizes.
corrections.caveats: First-party sample run on one unnamed Apple Silicon machine; modest gains (about 1.2-1.4x, a tie at N=256 forward). tinyfft is f32 while fft.js is f64 (round-trip error ~1e-7 vs ~1e-14), so precision differs; the bench README says so. Only fft.js is benchmarked although the bench describes 'popular JS/WASM FFT libraries'; no other wasm FFT (for example a pffft or KissFFT wasm build) is compared. The forward loop includes a 2N-float re-seed copy for tinyfft that fft.js does not pay. The scalar wasm build loses to fft.js, so the win depends on wasm SIMD. The live browser benchmark is on rluts.github.io (blocked here, not opened). 1 star, created mid-2026.

notes: Numbers match README and bench/README.md; bench/run.mjs verifies both backends against a naive DFT at N=256 before timing and the round-trip loop is copy-free on both sides, so the evidence is valid but modest. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1 star, last commit 2026-07-26.
